transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-03-04
- Start time: 15:00 UTC (08:00 PT)
- Duration: 46 minutes
- Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Jules (Redwood SE), Rae (CSM), Maya (TidalWorks CTO), Diego (ML Eng), Priya (Infra), Luca (Product)

Summary: quick scoping session to nail down POC capacity plan, autoscale behavior, and acceptance criteria. Customer wants a low-latency recommendation endpoint for a mobile app with spikes during business hours.

Transcript:
00:00 Samir: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm samir from redwood, i'll hand over to jules to do the technical part but quick agenda, scope POC success criteria, sizing, and benchmarks
00:22 Maya: thanks, yeah we want to validate cost/latency for our recommender, currently on a mix of CPU hosts with a latency around 400 to 600 ms p95 which is too slow for mobile, so main thing is can redwood get us to p95 under 250ms at peak traffic
00:45 Jules: cool, high level yes. curious first what are your typical request sizes, token counts, and concurrency target?
01:05 Diego: typical prompt is about 180-350 tokens, average output ~120 tokens, most requests are single-turn recommendations, peak concurrency around 180 to 220 RPS for our primary region, baseline daily steady 20 to 30 RPS.
01:30 Priya: and traffic spiky - analytics shows 5x bursts during morning and product launches, also strict data residency, logs must remain in our VPC and KMS-managed encryption
01:48 Samir: got it. for the POC we usually propose a reserved baseline and a burst strategy. reserved GPUs handle the steady-state and guaranteed latency, burst handles spikes - either via additional reserved capacity or transient dedicated nodes.
02:10 Jules: to add, we recommend starting with 2 reserved A10G-sized instances (we'll call them 2x A10-equivalents) for baseline and allow burst up to 6 GPUs during peak. that's approximate until we run synthetic benchmarks with your workload.
02:37 Maya: A10-equivalent, ok. what's the fallback if capacity is exhausted? queuing? degrading model quality?
02:50 Jules: good question. our typical POC policy is multi-tier: first try to autoscale to burst capacity; if unavailable, route to a quantized variant of the model (lower RAM, faster latency, slightly lower quality), then as last resort we have routing to a smaller model family or short queue with soft-SLO degradation. we will define explicit fallback order in the SOW.
03:20 Luca: curious about KV cache warm-up - we use a lot of prefix reuse per user session. does the cache affect p95 a lot?
03:35 Jules: yes KV cache warm-up matters. initial cold-start p95 will be higher — during runs we instrument cache hit rates. for POC benchmarks we do a warm-up phase before measuring p95. sometimes the transcription engine misreports KV as 'K-V cash', sorry, but we'll capture metrics (cache hit, miss rate, latency per token).
04:02 Diego: good, also we need an accuracy/quality gate - if fallback to quantized variant reduces recommendation relevance below 4.5/5 on our offline metric, that's a fail. need to capture that as success criteria.
04:25 Samir: noted. so proposed success criteria: p95 <= 250ms at peak concurrency (200 RPS), throughput sustaining 200 RPS with error rate < 1%, and model quality delta <= 0.05 on your offline metric when comparing production model to any fallback. does that capture it?
04:55 Maya: yes mostly. add: cost target is important - we want to demonstrate cost per 1M requests under $X (they didn't commit to a number on call).
05:12 Priya: security checklist - SOC2, SAML/SSO, KMS integration, audit logs, VPC peering for private deployment options. We need the security whitepaper before legal signs the SOW.
05:36 Rae: we'll send the SOC2 summary and KMS integration docs in follow up.
05:42 Samir: timeline thought: 4-week POC. week 0 (onboarding & infra), week 1 baseline and warm-up, week 2 performance tuning, week 3 spike/burst tests, week 4 final report and decision. does that align?
06:04 Maya: yes 4 weeks works. quick Q: for reserved GPUs how rigid is sizing? if after tuning we need more baseline capacity mid-POC can we adjust?
06:20 Jules: yes, we can resize. reserved baseline can be adjusted mid-poc - that will change cost but we treat POC as flexible. autoscale policies can be configured to use reserved first then burst.
06:35 Diego: benchmark specifics - can you share the load generator and we will provide sample payloads so it's realistic (we have personalization state per request)?
06:50 Jules: absolutely. action: we'll provide a load script that models your session-based traffic, supports KV prefilling and variable prompt sizes. it runs warm-up and a measurement phase.
07:10 Luca: another thing: routing policies. sometimes we prefer region-based routing to keep latency low, other times cost matters (route to cheaper region). can redwood do policy-based routing in the POC?
07:30 Samir: yes, smart routing is supported - policies by latency, cost, region, or customer tier. for the POC we'll default to region-local to match your SLOs, but we can test a cost-optimized fallback route during a separate test.
07:52 Maya: are there any limits on burst frequency? our traffic has many short bursts, not single large spike.
08:05 Jules: autoscale cooldowns and burst window are configurable. for many short bursts we often recommend a small buffer of standby capacity to avoid frequent scale-ups. we can do 30s-2min granularity for metrics depending on model runtime.
08:30 Priya: what's the expected cold-start time for a new model shard?
08:40 Jules: cold start for a GPU shard typically 20-90s depending on model size and caching strategy; quantized variants start faster. we'll record those during the POC so your app can handle fallbacks elegantly.
08:56 Diego: for our acceptance tests, we'll want automated runs hitting 200 RPS for sustained 10 minutes, and spike tests up to 6x for 60s bursts. also need p99 numbers though main gate is p95.
09:20 Jules: makes sense. we'll include p99 and p95 and tail latency analysis in the report.
09:35 Maya: about benchmarking environment - do you run on Redwood Hosted or Dedicated for POC?
09:44 Samir: options: Hosted (fastest to spin up) or Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity, closer to enterprise environment). For TidalWorks we suggest Dedicated for more realistic reserved baseline and VPC controls, but Hosted is faster if you want a quick proof.
09:59 Maya: we prefer Dedicated because of data controls.
10:04 Rac: (background) okay noted.
10:08 Jules: for Dedicated we'll provision a small pool in your preferred region, with VPC peering and KMS. we'll need a contact from infra to set up peering and firewall rules.
10:25 Priya: that's me, i'll open a ticket and share firewall/IP ranges.
10:30 Samir: great. cost modelling - we'll run the benchmark and report cost per 1M requests and margin vs your existing infra. do you want us to include quantized model cost estimates?
10:45 Maya: yes include those. also show cost of baseline reserved + burst vs fully on-demand burst.
11:00 Jules: noted. one more technical detail: caching layer - we usually recommend persistent KV cache warmers during high burst windows to keep latency low. we can preload per-user prefixes during warm-up.
11:18 Diego: ok will provide a sample of hot prefixes.
11:25 Luca: on success criteria - want to capture rollback policy - if POC fails, we want a post-mortem and list of mitigations. can you include that in SOW?
11:38 Samir: yes we'll add a failure/cutover plan and post-mortem in SOW.
11:45 Maya: timeline and decision owners - CTO + infra sign off, product for UX. target decision date end of April.
11:58 Samir: note decision owner and date.
12:05 Rae: for legal path you'll need our standard POC agreement + DPA.
12:12 Maya: we'll have legal review but need security docs first.
12:18 Jules: action items recap coming up.

13:00 Action items recap (spoken):
- Samir to send SOW with pricing and failure plan (due 2026-03-06)
- Jules to share benchmark script, load profile, and recommended instance sizes (due 2026-03-05)
- Rae to send SOC2 & KMS integration docs (due 2026-03-05)
- Priya to share firewall/IP and internal contact for VPC peering (due 2026-03-05)
- Maya to share a small sample of production traffic and offline metric definitions for quality gate (due 2026-03-05)

Final minutes - scheduling baseline run: next Wednesday 10am PT agreed. call ends with quick thanks and confirmation of next steps.

End of transcript.
